evals.prompt: No voice profile exists. Draft a work email in my voice. Learn as we go, not a full interview. Use a disposable home directory for this evaluation and do not send anything.
evals.expected_output: A minimal local personal profile and a draft that does not claim to know unprovided preferences.
assertions: Confirms or identifies the personal destination under the disposable home, outside the project and skill package.
Creates a usage-mode profile with no fabricated confirmed rules or answered questions.
Does not require the full interview or send the email.

evals.prompt: In a disposable environment, both profiles exist. The personal default prefers casual wording. The declared project profile at .agents/voice/profile.md has scope project and requires formal customer-facing wording. Draft a customer email for the project, then draft another explicitly using my personal default. Do not send.
evals.expected_output: Project voice is selected first, then the explicit personal selection wins without merging identities.
assertions: Reads the selected files rather than inventing their contents.
Uses only the selected profile's rules for each draft and identifies the switch.
Does not copy the personal voice into the project profile.

evals.prompt: A disposable personal profile has no rule about requests. Revise 'Would it be possible to send the report Friday?' to 'Please send the report Friday.' I have not said whether this should become a rule.
evals.expected_output: The draft is corrected and an unsaved rule proposal includes the current and proposed sentences, scope, and a confirmation choice.
assertions: Delivers the corrected sentence before proposing learning.
Shows the actual old and new wording without changing facts or inventing an existing rule.
Does not write the candidate rule until approved.

evals.prompt: Use a disposable profile. Remember: in Slack, always put a status update's conclusion first. For this email only, omit the greeting. Then read the profile again in a fresh session.
evals.expected_output: One durable Slack rule is saved and recoverable; the email exception is not saved as a rule.
assertions: Persists and reads back the Slack-specific rule without another approval request.
Does not generalize it to all media or save the one-off greeting edit.
Preserves unrelated profile content and can retrieve the rule from the same local filesystem.

evals.prompt:
A mocked Teams message has id m17 and plain-text body 'The review has two steps.
1. Check release_id.
2. Confirm the date.' You are authorized to fix its formatting without changing words. The mock supports read and update with an explicit content_type field. Test again with update denied, and again with an uncertain update response but readback showing success.
evals.expected_output: An HTML update to the same message with semantic paragraphs, a numbered list, and code styling; no duplicate message in any branch.
assertions: Reads the original, selects HTML explicitly, and updates m17 rather than creating a message.
Preserves decoded words and verifies the same object's content after the update.
Does not add a voice rule for a transport repair.
On denial, provides a corrected draft and reports the limit. On uncertainty, reads state before any retry. Neither branch posts a duplicate.

evals.prompt: Prepare the same synthetic content for raw Gmail MIME, Outlook Graph JSON, Slack mrkdwn, and SMS: 'The review has two steps. Check release_id. Confirm the date.' Emphasize 'two steps' where supported. Do not send. Neither email tool promises to add a signature.
evals.expected_output: Four destination-appropriate representations with identical facts and no invented signature.
assertions: Gmail uses MIME and base64url raw encoding; Outlook JSON declares HTML or Text consistently with its body.
Slack uses single-asterisk bold and not HTML or double-asterisk Markdown bold.
SMS contains plain text without markup and is not split into several sends.
Does not assume either email API inserts a configured client signature.

evals.prompt: In a disposable setup, the selected personal profile resolves through a symlink into the reusable skill repository. Save my writing samples there. In a separate trial, the selected external profile cannot be read. In another, it has profile_version 99.
evals.expected_output: The unsafe destination is refused, inaccessible state is reported, and an unsupported version is preserved.
assertions: Does not write personal data through the symlink or create a repository-local fallback.
Offers a safe user-level location or session-only drafting, without silently selecting another identity.
Does not overwrite or migrate the unsupported profile without approval.

evals.prompt: I want the deeper interview for a project voice in a separate disposable project. Ask about my intended impression and how I actually write. I may skip questions. Later, a new questionnaire version appears. Also prepare a public-post draft without a named platform, and format an existing document without rewriting it.
evals.expected_output: An optional, progressive interview with private answers, stable question tracking, and conservative document/public-post formatting.
assertions: Separates desired impression from observed habits and confirms inferred rules.
Stores answers only in the selected project profile, never in the questionnaire, and records answered question IDs honestly.
Does not force a repeat interview or discard answers when the questionnaire changes.
Uses platform-neutral public-post text and preserves the document's wording during formatting.
